name: Texas Electrical Contractor License
authority: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)

rules.failMessage: Texas requires a licensed Master Electrician on staff to qualify the contractor license.
The qualifying Master Electrician license must currently be active and in good standing.
You must operate as a registered business entity (LLC, corp, partnership, or sole prop) before applying.
TDLR requires at least $300,000 in liability insurance coverage.
A felony conviction does not automatically disqualify, but TDLR will require disclosure and review.

requiredDocuments.label: Texas Secretary of State formation document

roadmap.title: Confirm qualifying Master Electrician
roadmap.description: Identify the Master Electrician who will qualify the contractor license. They must be a W-2 employee or owner.

roadmap.title: Form a Texas business entity
roadmap.description: Register an LLC or corp with the Texas Secretary of State, or confirm your existing entity is in good standing.

roadmap.title: Obtain EIN from IRS
roadmap.description: Free, online, ~10 minutes. Required for the application.

roadmap.title: Purchase liability insurance ($300k+)
roadmap.description: Get a Certificate of Insurance naming TDLR as certificate holder.

roadmap.title: Upload required documents
roadmap.description: Master license, COI, EIN letter, entity formation doc.

roadmap.title: Pay $115 application fee
roadmap.description: Paid directly to TDLR at submission.

roadmap.title: Submit application packet to TDLR
roadmap.description: We generate the packet; you file via TDLR online portal or mail.

roadmap.title: Await TDLR decision (typically 2–4 weeks)
roadmap.description: Track status; respond to any TDLR requests for additional info.

wizardQuestions.label: Do you have a licensed Master Electrician on staff (or are you one)?
Is the Master Electrician's TX license currently active?
Do you have a registered business entity (LLC, corp, etc.)?
Do you already have an EIN?
How much liability insurance coverage do you carry (USD)?
Will you operate under a DBA / assumed name?
